值得閱讀的理由

  • 深刻剖析孫中山五權憲法獨立考試權與監察權的憲政遠見，理解制度防腐與品質管控的必要性。
  • 以1881年美國總統加菲爾遇刺案為例，透析早期西方民主分贓制（獵官制）引發的體制災難與文官改革歷程。
  • 對比當前中共「黨管幹部」的政治運作，揭示政治忠誠凌駕專業理性所帶來的深層治理浩劫。

摘要

民主機器的隱患與五權憲法的防腐機制

作者藉由超跑與遙控器的生動比喻指出，人民手中握有選舉、罷免、創制、複決等權利，如同持有高級跑車的遙控器，但若政府機器內部零件粗製濫造、滿布鏽斑，僅憑選民的控制依然無法防止車輛失控。國父早在百餘年前便洞悉此一問題，認為僅有西方傳統的三權分立仍有漏洞，因而提出將考試權與監察權獨立出來。考試權負責政府人才的品質把關，監察權則負責內部的防腐監督。作者強調，此一見解與現代憲政學者艾克曼的理論不謀而合，證明了民主不僅是投票制度，更需要一套實質的防腐劑與穩定器。

美國「獵官制」的歷史悲劇與三大災難

作者回顧了1881年美國總統加菲爾遇刺身亡的歷史慘劇，直指其背後的罪魁禍首正是惡名昭彰的分贓制。在早期美國政治中，「勝者全拿官職」成為潛規則，競選功臣與金主得以瓜分內閣及各級官職。作者引述國父的分析，點出該體制造成的「三大災難」：其一是效能週期性崩潰，每次政黨輪替導致政府如走馬燈般陷入混亂；其二是逆向淘汰，選邊站的政客取代了具備專業能力的專家；其三則是體制性腐敗，公職淪為政治投資的籌碼，官員只向賜官的政黨效忠而非國家。雖然美國隨後在1883年通過《彭德爾頓法案》設立文官委員會，但國父認為文官系統若受制於行政權，防火牆終究存在後門，必須拉高至憲法位階才能徹底杜絕分贓。

從分贓制到極權實踐：現代「黨管幹部」的代價

作者進一步將歷史上的獵官制延伸對照當今中共體制，指出其「黨管幹部」本質上是更徹底、全面且永久的政治恩庇。從政府、國企到學術機構，所有核心職位皆由黨組織掌控分配。雖然這種模式看似避免了定期輪替造成的行政中斷，但其穩定背後付出的代價極其高昂。首要病灶便是專業理性被扼殺，當「政治忠誠」成為升遷首要考量，技術官僚的專業判斷被迫屈服於領袖意志，導致如大躍進或動態清零等重大決策失誤；其次則是派系依附取代制度理性，徹底扭曲了健全官僚體系的運作。

================================================

Hello! Everyone. This is A-Niu. The third part of "Lecture Six on Democracy." In the previous two episodes we finished discussing. "the distinction between power and ability." To understand it better,. let us give an example. You just bought a supercar,. holding the remote control of this car in your hand. You can start it at any time,. turn it off at any time. But if you open the hood and look,. and to your surprise the engine parts are all made of plastic,. the oil lines full of rust,. would you still dare to step on the gas? What we want to ask today is:. relying only on the remote control in the people's hands,. can it really guarantee that the. "all-powerful government" will not have problems? The Founding Father actually, over 100 years ago,. already saw this problem. He said. that the people having election,. recall,. initiative,. and referendum is not enough. Why? First,. if the people who go into the government to do the work. got in by connections,. then the parts of this machine. are inferior goods from the day they leave the factory. Second,. if inside the machine. no one continuously monitors or supervises,. then corruption and malpractice, like rust,. will slowly corrode the entire circuit from the inside. By the time the people feel something is wrong. and want to press the remote control,. this car may long ago have been unable to brake. So he pulled the "examination" and "supervisory" powers. out of the traditional three powers (executive, legislative, judicial). to stand independently. The examination power is responsible for quality control,. ensuring that the people entering the government. have real talent and learning. The supervisory power is responsible. for rust-proofing or anti-corrosion,. continuously monitoring and supervising inside the government. But you might think,. isn't this just nostalgia? Taking China's traditional imperial examinations,. the censorate, and such systems,. and moving them into modern politics. But the core of the problem he truly aimed at. was two loopholes that 19th-century Western democracy. exposed. The prescription he himself wrote. The interesting thing is. that in the year 2000,. American constitutional scholar Ackerman. was almost completely consistent. with this logic of the Founding Father. We can put it this way:. democracy is not just a voting system. It also needs a set of anti-corrosives and stabilizers. This is, in the Five-Power Constitution,. the most underrated insight. So what exactly did the Founding Father see back then. in terms of the ills of Western democracy? As the story goes, in 1881,. the American president took a train to the station,. and a man who had failed to obtain office pulled out a gun. The then American president Garfield was assassinated. This was not a random killing,. but a tragedy caused by a. "spoils system." Someone treated public office like a lottery ticket,. and when they could not cash in the prize,. they poured their rage into bullets. A system so rotten. that it made people risk their lives to grab official posts. I think this kind of tragedy. is one no one wants to happen. Let us examine carefully. the institutional problem. behind the American president's assassination. How exactly did America's "spoils system" operate? When the Founding Father gave his lectures,. he spent great effort on one thing:. performing a pathological dissection of Western democracy. His attitude was not anti-democracy,. but rather to say:.

your separation of three powers has loopholes,. and I want to patch up the loopholes. The first disease is America's "spoils system." What is the spoils system? In plain terms it is:. win the election,. and all the official posts in the country. are the president's spoils of war,. rewarded according to merit and distributed to his own people. This way of playing,. in the era when Jackson served as American president,. became an explicit rule. Their slogan was:. "To the victor belong the spoils." What does it mean? You help me canvass votes to win the presidency,. and I give you a lucrative customs post. You donate a lot of money,. and I make you the postmaster. From cabinet ministers to minor local officials,. all are spoils the president distributes down. The Founding Father observed that this system. would bring three disasters. The first disaster. is called the periodic collapse of effectiveness. A general election is held every 4 years. No matter who is elected,. the government gets a major blood transfusion. The newly arrived people do not understand the business at all,. and before they have even figured out which way the door opens,. the next term must change people again. In his lecture he gave a metaphor:. the government spins like a revolving lantern,. forever in handover,. forever in chaos. The second disaster is called "reverse elimination." What kind of people can become officials? Not the most capable people,. but the people best at picking sides. No matter how strong your professional ability,. if you have no party card,. you cannot even get in the door. Conversely,. those old hands in the politician circles,. the election campaign fixers,. sit down in the offices one by one. The Founding Father's principle is very clear:. governing power should be given to experts,. not to loyal followers. The third disaster is the most serious,. and that is systemic corruption. Think about it. If a person's official post. is a gift given by the party,. to whom will they be accountable after taking office? To the party,. accountable to their benefactor,. not to the country,. accountable to the law. And to get this post,. they may have spent a sum of money to "buy" it. So what will they do after taking office? Of course, recover that money. Public office becomes an investment target,. and corruption goes from an individual case. to the normal state of the entire system. This spoils system, later on,. the Americans really could not stand it. So,. after that presidential assassination in 1881,. it ultimately forced out the pressure for necessary reform. In 1883,. the US Congress passed the "Pendleton Act," establishing the Civil Service Commission. and beginning to adopt a system. of selecting talent through examinations. However, after the Founding Father looked at it, he said. this was not enough. Why? Because your Civil Service Commission. is a bureau hung under the executive branch. The president still has ways to apply pressure,. the ruling party still has channels to stuff in its own people. If the examination power. does not break away from the executive power. to independently become a. constitutional organ parallel to. the executive,. judicial, and legislative powers,. then the firewall will forever have a back door. That gunshot in America. also shattered a myth:. that relying on elections alone can produce good government. But the Founding Father actually saw farther than the Americans. He wanted not only a "merit system,"

but to upgrade the merit system into. a constitutional-level institutional firewall,. so that no political party could treat the civil service system. as its own backyard garden. In short,. elections decide who drives the car,. but examinations decide. how this car's parts are assembled. If you give the power to build the car to elections,. then sooner or later you will sit in a useless cobbled-together car. Although in the 19th century. America's spoils system was already outrageous,. even today in the 21st century. there are still people who play this way of doing things. to the extreme. Permanently,. comprehensively dividing the spoils. From government to enterprises to schools,. all sectors are dividing the spoils. As long as you are not a party member,. you cannot get a share of the pie. If the spoils system is permanent,. comprehensive,. distributed from the central government. down to the neighborhood committee at the end of your alley,. from the chairman of a state-owned enterprise down. to the university president,. what kind of scene would that be? No need to imagine. This system is operating today. It even has an official name,. called "the Party manages cadres." Is the CCP's "Party manages cadres" essentially the same thing as. America's early spoils system? When the Founding Father. criticized America's spoils system back then,. the core concept he used. can be summarized in four characters:. political patronage. It means. your official post was not earned by ability,. but bestowed on you by political power. To whom are you loyal? Loyal to the person who gave you the post. The American version is that you win the election. before you can divide the spoils. Four years later it may have to be reshuffled. But the CCP's version is more thorough. It does not need elections,. one party rules permanently. So the division of spoils is not a one-time thing,. it is a normal state written into the system. All key positions:. government,. enterprises,. schools,. social organizations,. are all inspected and appointed. by the Party's Organization Department. Of course you might say. at least this system is stable,. it will not have a major blood. transfusion every four years like America. Correct. It indeed avoids the problem of administrative interruption. But what is the price of stability? There are at least three deeper root diseases. The first root disease is. that professional rationality is smothered alive. When "political loyalty" becomes the first metric of assessment,. the professional judgment of technical bureaucrats. must give way to political directives. When the experts say no. and the leader says yes,. who should be obeyed? Of course, obey the leader. As a result,. the Great Leap Forward of 1958 came about this way. The dynamic-zero policy during the pandemic. also came about this way. It is not that no one saw the problem,. it is that even if someone saw the problem, they dared not speak,. or were disappeared. Because if you spoke up, you were no longer loyal. The second root disease is. that factional dependence replaces institutional rationality. In a normal modern bureaucratic system,. promotion relies on performance,. on rules,. on "impersonal" standards. But in the Party-manages-cadres system,. if you want promotion,. you must first find a big tree.

Your future lies not in what you have done,. but in who the person you follow is. This forms. layer upon layer of factional networks. You promote me,. I promote him,. and the whole system becomes a web of relationships. rather than a professional machine. The third root disease is also the most fatal,. and that is the complete failure of supervision. The Discipline Inspection Commission responsible for supervision. and the officials being supervised. have the same boss above their heads:. the Party (the Chinese Communist Party). This is like a football match where. the referee,. the players,. and the coach all wear the same jersey. Do you want the referee to blow the whistle and catch fouls? The ones he catches are always the opposing team. When his own people foul, he pretends not to see. So you will find. that the CCP's anti-corruption campaigns. forever carry a strong flavor of factional struggle. Anti-corruption campaigns always strike political rivals,. not corrupt officials. So what is the Founding Father's solution? It is actually the independence of the examination power. His intent is very clear:. to draw, between "political power" and "the civil service system," a line that cannot be crossed. The Party can govern,. but the Party cannot stuff its own people. into the civil service ranks. The Party can set policy direction,. but cannot order civil servants. to violate professional ethics in execution. The recruitment of civil servants,. promotion,. performance evaluation,. must be the responsibility of a constitutional organ. independent of any political party. Placed in today's context, this statement. is the sharpest knife for deconstructing. "the Party manages cadres." America's spoils division is short-term,. the CCP's Party-manages-cadres is permanent. Although the two differ in form,. the root disease is the same:. both have politics devouring professionalism. The Founding Father, over a hundred years ago,. already saw through this structural problem. Everyone has probably seen "Shaolin Soccer." There is a scene in it where it says:. the referee,. the umpire,. the linesman,. the technical committee member,. the organizer,. the co-organizer,. all the units are my people,. how can you fight against me? The Founding Father said. this was the real state. of Western parliaments at the end of the 19th century. Members of parliament are themselves political contenders. If you let them simultaneously be the referee,. to impeach executive officials,. then every whistle they blow. is based on partisan interest. The Founding Father's second knife. cut at a rarely questioned assumption. within the Western separation of three powers:. that the impeachment power and the investigative power. should, as a matter of course, belong to parliament. Britain is like this,. America is also like this. But the Founding Father said:. wait a moment. There are two big problems here. The first problem is called the weaponization of power. This thing called impeachment,. what was the original intent of its design? It is the last line of defense of the democratic system. When an official seriously breaks the law,. the people's representatives launch impeachment. to pull him down. But how does it actually work in practice? Members of parliament discovered. that the impeachment power is a very useful stick. I do not need to actually beat you out of office. I only need to raise the stick and wave it,. and you must listen to me,. let my bill pass,.

allocate funds to my district. The Founding Father called this "parliamentary tyranny." Parliament is not supervising the executive,. but extorting the executive branch. Has this phenomenon disappeared today? We look at many Latin American countries,. where the president clashes with parliament,. and parliament launches impeachment at every turn,. like Brazil and Peru,. how many presidents have been impeached in recent years. You can also look at South Korea,. where impeachment has almost become a standard procedure. that every South Korean president must go through. Even America itself,. the way impeachment cases. have been operated in the past few years. also increasingly resembles parties. tossing grenades at each other. rather than maintaining constitutional order. The Founding Father's diagnosis over a hundred years ago. is still valid today. The second problem is more fundamental:. the supervisors themselves have conflicts of interest. Who are members of parliament? They are not saints fallen from heaven. They themselves are members of political parties,. participants in political interests. If you let a player double as the referee,. how can he possibly be fair? When investigating officials of the opposing party,. he is especially diligent,. especially high-profile. If you ask him to investigate officials of his own party? Usually it is gently set down,. quietly passed over. This is not a character problem,. this is a structural problem. Because the institutional design. put the supervisors and the supervised. in the same field of interest. How can you expect him to be detached? So the Founding Father's solution is very clear:. take the supervisory power,. including impeachment, censure, and audit,. the whole set out of parliament's hands,. and set it up as an independent governing organ,. that is, the "supervisory power." This organ does not take orders from the president,. so it will not have officials shielding officials. It is also not subject to parliament,. so it will not become a weapon of vicious partisan struggle. It is simply an independent referee,. accountable only to the constitution,. accountable only to the cleanliness of the system. You can think carefully:. this design happens to form, with the people's recall power,. a "double insurance." The people watch from the outside. If you do not do well,. I use the ballot to replace you,. use recall to pull you down. This is external supervision. The Control Yuan watches from the inside. If you embezzle,. I impeach you. If you neglect your duty,. I censure you. This is internal supervision. One line of defense outside,. one line of defense inside. The two added together. can truly contain that "all-powerful government." The Founding Father's meaning is very clear:. the referee cannot place bets. If you want to supervise the government,. you must find someone who has no. political stake of their own to do it. Leaving the impeachment power in parliament. is equivalent to letting gamblers be the referee. Making the supervisory power independent. is what brings the game back to the rules. Simply put, democracy needs a referee,. but the referee cannot go onto the field to play. This is the reason the supervisory power must be independent. The Founding Father found the lesion from the West,. and also wrote the prescription. And the prescription was not fabricated out of thin air,. but came from looking back at China's own history,. discovering that our ancestors. had actually already tried something similar. Next we will talk about China's own system. As the story goes, in 1624,. during the Tianqi reign of the Ming dynasty,. a censor named Yang Lian,. knowing full well that offending Wei Zhongxian.

was equivalent to courting death,. still submitted an impeachment memorial,. listing twenty-four major crimes. As a result he was thrown into the imperial prison,. tormented to death alive. But do you know? Although he died,. the institution of the Censorate did not die. Three years later Wei Zhongxian fell,. and the whole supervisory system turned again. A single person can be killed,. but if an institution is designed firmly enough,. even eunuch dictatorship cannot crush it. What the Founding Father saw was precisely this. Is the supervisory power nostalgia or innovation? Between China's traditional censor system. and modern constitutional theory,. does there exist a logical line that connects them? Let us first return to history. The Control Yuan that the Founding Father designed,. its prototype is the Censorate and the Court of Censors. American sinologist Charles Hucker. specifically studied the Ming dynasty supervisory system. He gave it a very high evaluation,. calling it "the traditional mainstay." It means this system. is the skeleton supporting the operation of the entire empire. Hucker pointed out. that the Ming dynasty supervisory system. has three features worth noting. The first is a full-coverage monitoring network. This group of censors. had their own independent intelligence channels. In ancient China there was a saying called "speaking on hearsay," meaning I do not even. need to see ironclad evidence with my own eyes. As long as I hear word of something,. I can submit a memorial of impeachment,. and investigate afterward. From the central Six Ministries to local prefectures and counties,. the tentacles of supervision were everywhere. The second is dual function. Censors not only watched officials below,. they could also remonstrate with the emperor above. In theory he was both the inspection corps. that disciplined the officials. and the one who stepped on the brakes against monarchical power. Of course,. in practice the power of remonstrance was often discounted. But at least in institutional design,. the supervisory power had the intent to check the highest power. The third, and what most surprised Hucker,. was the resilience of the system. In the late Ming, Wei Zhongxian monopolized power,. and the eunuch faction wildly purged the censors,. killing some,. demoting some. But even in those darkest days,. the basic skeleton of the supervisory system. did not completely disintegrate. Yang Lian died,. but the institution of impeachment still existed. Individual censors were suppressed,. but the performance-evaluation mechanism still operated. After the storm passed,. the system restarted again. A system that can survive the crushing of extreme politics,. this shows that its design itself. has structural value. But here there is a fatal key point,. and that is "but." The source of power. of the traditional censor system was the emperor. The censor was "the eyes and ears of imperial power," not "the guardian of the people." When the emperor was wise,. the censor was a sharp weapon. But when the emperor was muddleheaded,. or was hollowed out by eunuchs,. the censor became a decoration, or even a sacrificial victim. The Founding Father's true innovation lies right here. He pulled this traditional organ's power cord. out of "imperial bestowal" and plugged it into "the people's bestowal," letting the legitimacy of the supervisory power. come from the constitution,. come from the people,. not from any single person. This way the nature of the whole system. went from a tool of emperors. to infrastructure of democracy. Let us talk again about another. viewpoint of contemporary Western constitutional theory. It comes from America,. from Yale Law School constitutional scholar Ackerman.

In our previous discussions of Democracy. we also introduced his viewpoint. In line with the discussion context of the supervisory power,. we still cite his viewpoint. Ackerman once published a. heavyweight legal paper named. "The New Separation of Powers." The viewpoint of this article. and the viewpoint the Founding Father proposed. 76 years before him. actually have astonishing similarities. It shows the Founding Father. had the power to penetrate across eras. Ackerman's core argument is. that the traditional separation of three powers is no longer enough. The modern state is too complex. You cannot stuff every function into. the executive,. legislative,. judicial,. three boxes. He proposed that modern constitutions. need to add two new independent branches. The first is called the "integrity branch," specifically responsible for fighting corruption. This institution must have a constitutionally guaranteed budget,. members must have a high degree of tenure protection,. and absolutely cannot be appointed solely by the president. or the executive chief. The only purpose of its existence. is to watch whether anyone in the government. is stealing,. cheating,. using power for private gain. This is almost the same blueprint. as the Founding Father's supervisory power. The second is called the "regulatory branch," specifically protecting professional decisions. from being distorted by politicians. How to do environmental protection,. how to set financial regulation,. these things need professional knowledge. You cannot let short-sighted politicians. change them recklessly for the sake of votes. So you need an independent institution. to hold the professional bottom line. This is the examination power. The spirit of the examination power. is not just holding examinations,. but ensuring that "governing power" is held. in the hands of people who truly have professional ability,. not contaminated by political force. Two people,. two eras,. two completely different intellectual traditions,. yet drew almost identical institutional blueprints. The Founding Father in 1924. proposed the Five-Power Constitution. Ackerman in 2000,. from the predicament of contemporary democracy,. deduced a new separation-of-powers theory. The two reached the same conclusion by different paths. In academic language,. the Five-Power Constitution is actually. a pioneer of "functional separation of powers." What he wanted to do is very clear:. take the two functions a modern state most needs,. "professionalism" and "integrity," pull them out of the chaotic political mudslinging,. and put them into a constitutional-level safe box. The Ming dynasty's Yang Lian. used his life to protect the dignity of the censors,. but he could not protect the root of the institution,. because that root was planted in the soil of imperial power. What the Founding Father did. was uproot the same tree. and transplant it into the soil of contemporary democracy. Ackerman, 76 years later,. came from a completely different direction. and planted an almost identical tree. The same answer was, by two eras,. two civilizations' thinkers,. each independently deduced. This is not coincidence but inevitability. The independent guarantee of professionalism and integrity. is a necessity of the modern state. Because the Three Principles of the People. are actually very much worth discussing,. but the content is really too much. We will discuss in the next episode. the unique institutional design of the "Five-Power Constitution," that is, the examination power and the supervisory power,. and will also introduce their practical experience in Taiwan,. hoping to make a modest contribution to how a future China,. after democratization, should carry out constitutional design.

If you enjoyed this episode,. please like,. subscribe, and share it. So we will see you next time. Bye bye!

值得閱讀的理由

  • 深刻剖析孫中山五權憲法獨立考試權與監察權的憲政遠見，理解制度防腐與品質管控的必要性。
  • 以1881年美國總統加菲爾遇刺案為例，透析早期西方民主分贓制（獵官制）引發的體制災難與文官改革歷程。
  • 對比當前中共「黨管幹部」的政治運作，揭示政治忠誠凌駕專業理性所帶來的深層治理浩劫。

摘要

民主機器的隱患與五權憲法的防腐機制

作者藉由超跑與遙控器的生動比喻指出，人民手中握有選舉、罷免、創制、複決等權利，如同持有高級跑車的遙控器，但若政府機器內部零件粗製濫造、滿布鏽斑，僅憑選民的控制依然無法防止車輛失控。國父早在百餘年前便洞悉此一問題，認為僅有西方傳統的三權分立仍有漏洞，因而提出將考試權與監察權獨立出來。考試權負責政府人才的品質把關，監察權則負責內部的防腐監督。作者強調，此一見解與現代憲政學者艾克曼的理論不謀而合，證明了民主不僅是投票制度，更需要一套實質的防腐劑與穩定器。

美國「獵官制」的歷史悲劇與三大災難

作者回顧了1881年美國總統加菲爾遇刺身亡的歷史慘劇，直指其背後的罪魁禍首正是惡名昭彰的分贓制。在早期美國政治中，「勝者全拿官職」成為潛規則，競選功臣與金主得以瓜分內閣及各級官職。作者引述國父的分析，點出該體制造成的「三大災難」：其一是效能週期性崩潰，每次政黨輪替導致政府如走馬燈般陷入混亂；其二是逆向淘汰，選邊站的政客取代了具備專業能力的專家；其三則是體制性腐敗，公職淪為政治投資的籌碼，官員只向賜官的政黨效忠而非國家。雖然美國隨後在1883年通過《彭德爾頓法案》設立文官委員會，但國父認為文官系統若受制於行政權，防火牆終究存在後門，必須拉高至憲法位階才能徹底杜絕分贓。

從分贓制到極權實踐：現代「黨管幹部」的代價

作者進一步將歷史上的獵官制延伸對照當今中共體制，指出其「黨管幹部」本質上是更徹底、全面且永久的政治恩庇。從政府、國企到學術機構，所有核心職位皆由黨組織掌控分配。雖然這種模式看似避免了定期輪替造成的行政中斷，但其穩定背後付出的代價極其高昂。首要病灶便是專業理性被扼殺，當「政治忠誠」成為升遷首要考量，技術官僚的專業判斷被迫屈服於領袖意志，導致如大躍進或動態清零等重大決策失誤；其次則是派系依附取代制度理性，徹底扭曲了健全官僚體系的運作。

================================================

Hello! Everyone. This is A-Niu. The third part of "Lecture Six on Democracy." In the previous two episodes we finished discussing. "the distinction between power and ability." To understand it better,. let us give an example. You just bought a supercar,. holding the remote control of this car in your hand. You can start it at any time,. turn it off at any time. But if you open the hood and look,. and to your surprise the engine parts are all made of plastic,. the oil lines full of rust,. would you still dare to step on the gas? What we want to ask today is:. relying only on the remote control in the people's hands,. can it really guarantee that the. "all-powerful government" will not have problems? The Founding Father actually, over 100 years ago,. already saw this problem. He said. that the people having election,. recall,. initiative,. and referendum is not enough. Why? First,. if the people who go into the government to do the work. got in by connections,. then the parts of this machine. are inferior goods from the day they leave the factory. Second,. if inside the machine. no one continuously monitors or supervises,. then corruption and malpractice, like rust,. will slowly corrode the entire circuit from the inside. By the time the people feel something is wrong. and want to press the remote control,. this car may long ago have been unable to brake. So he pulled the "examination" and "supervisory" powers. out of the traditional three powers (executive, legislative, judicial). to stand independently. The examination power is responsible for quality control,. ensuring that the people entering the government. have real talent and learning. The supervisory power is responsible. for rust-proofing or anti-corrosion,. continuously monitoring and supervising inside the government. But you might think,. isn't this just nostalgia? Taking China's traditional imperial examinations,. the censorate, and such systems,. and moving them into modern politics. But the core of the problem he truly aimed at. was two loopholes that 19th-century Western democracy. exposed. The prescription he himself wrote. The interesting thing is. that in the year 2000,. American constitutional scholar Ackerman. was almost completely consistent. with this logic of the Founding Father. We can put it this way:. democracy is not just a voting system. It also needs a set of anti-corrosives and stabilizers. This is, in the Five-Power Constitution,. the most underrated insight. So what exactly did the Founding Father see back then. in terms of the ills of Western democracy? As the story goes, in 1881,. the American president took a train to the station,. and a man who had failed to obtain office pulled out a gun. The then American president Garfield was assassinated. This was not a random killing,. but a tragedy caused by a. "spoils system." Someone treated public office like a lottery ticket,. and when they could not cash in the prize,. they poured their rage into bullets. A system so rotten. that it made people risk their lives to grab official posts. I think this kind of tragedy. is one no one wants to happen. Let us examine carefully. the institutional problem. behind the American president's assassination. How exactly did America's "spoils system" operate? When the Founding Father gave his lectures,. he spent great effort on one thing:. performing a pathological dissection of Western democracy. His attitude was not anti-democracy,. but rather to say:.

your separation of three powers has loopholes,. and I want to patch up the loopholes. The first disease is America's "spoils system." What is the spoils system? In plain terms it is:. win the election,. and all the official posts in the country. are the president's spoils of war,. rewarded according to merit and distributed to his own people. This way of playing,. in the era when Jackson served as American president,. became an explicit rule. Their slogan was:. "To the victor belong the spoils." What does it mean? You help me canvass votes to win the presidency,. and I give you a lucrative customs post. You donate a lot of money,. and I make you the postmaster. From cabinet ministers to minor local officials,. all are spoils the president distributes down. The Founding Father observed that this system. would bring three disasters. The first disaster. is called the periodic collapse of effectiveness. A general election is held every 4 years. No matter who is elected,. the government gets a major blood transfusion. The newly arrived people do not understand the business at all,. and before they have even figured out which way the door opens,. the next term must change people again. In his lecture he gave a metaphor:. the government spins like a revolving lantern,. forever in handover,. forever in chaos. The second disaster is called "reverse elimination." What kind of people can become officials? Not the most capable people,. but the people best at picking sides. No matter how strong your professional ability,. if you have no party card,. you cannot even get in the door. Conversely,. those old hands in the politician circles,. the election campaign fixers,. sit down in the offices one by one. The Founding Father's principle is very clear:. governing power should be given to experts,. not to loyal followers. The third disaster is the most serious,. and that is systemic corruption. Think about it. If a person's official post. is a gift given by the party,. to whom will they be accountable after taking office? To the party,. accountable to their benefactor,. not to the country,. accountable to the law. And to get this post,. they may have spent a sum of money to "buy" it. So what will they do after taking office? Of course, recover that money. Public office becomes an investment target,. and corruption goes from an individual case. to the normal state of the entire system. This spoils system, later on,. the Americans really could not stand it. So,. after that presidential assassination in 1881,. it ultimately forced out the pressure for necessary reform. In 1883,. the US Congress passed the "Pendleton Act," establishing the Civil Service Commission. and beginning to adopt a system. of selecting talent through examinations. However, after the Founding Father looked at it, he said. this was not enough. Why? Because your Civil Service Commission. is a bureau hung under the executive branch. The president still has ways to apply pressure,. the ruling party still has channels to stuff in its own people. If the examination power. does not break away from the executive power. to independently become a. constitutional organ parallel to. the executive,. judicial, and legislative powers,. then the firewall will forever have a back door. That gunshot in America. also shattered a myth:. that relying on elections alone can produce good government. But the Founding Father actually saw farther than the Americans. He wanted not only a "merit system,"

but to upgrade the merit system into. a constitutional-level institutional firewall,. so that no political party could treat the civil service system. as its own backyard garden. In short,. elections decide who drives the car,. but examinations decide. how this car's parts are assembled. If you give the power to build the car to elections,. then sooner or later you will sit in a useless cobbled-together car. Although in the 19th century. America's spoils system was already outrageous,. even today in the 21st century. there are still people who play this way of doing things. to the extreme. Permanently,. comprehensively dividing the spoils. From government to enterprises to schools,. all sectors are dividing the spoils. As long as you are not a party member,. you cannot get a share of the pie. If the spoils system is permanent,. comprehensive,. distributed from the central government. down to the neighborhood committee at the end of your alley,. from the chairman of a state-owned enterprise down. to the university president,. what kind of scene would that be? No need to imagine. This system is operating today. It even has an official name,. called "the Party manages cadres." Is the CCP's "Party manages cadres" essentially the same thing as. America's early spoils system? When the Founding Father. criticized America's spoils system back then,. the core concept he used. can be summarized in four characters:. political patronage. It means. your official post was not earned by ability,. but bestowed on you by political power. To whom are you loyal? Loyal to the person who gave you the post. The American version is that you win the election. before you can divide the spoils. Four years later it may have to be reshuffled. But the CCP's version is more thorough. It does not need elections,. one party rules permanently. So the division of spoils is not a one-time thing,. it is a normal state written into the system. All key positions:. government,. enterprises,. schools,. social organizations,. are all inspected and appointed. by the Party's Organization Department. Of course you might say. at least this system is stable,. it will not have a major blood. transfusion every four years like America. Correct. It indeed avoids the problem of administrative interruption. But what is the price of stability? There are at least three deeper root diseases. The first root disease is. that professional rationality is smothered alive. When "political loyalty" becomes the first metric of assessment,. the professional judgment of technical bureaucrats. must give way to political directives. When the experts say no. and the leader says yes,. who should be obeyed? Of course, obey the leader. As a result,. the Great Leap Forward of 1958 came about this way. The dynamic-zero policy during the pandemic. also came about this way. It is not that no one saw the problem,. it is that even if someone saw the problem, they dared not speak,. or were disappeared. Because if you spoke up, you were no longer loyal. The second root disease is. that factional dependence replaces institutional rationality. In a normal modern bureaucratic system,. promotion relies on performance,. on rules,. on "impersonal" standards. But in the Party-manages-cadres system,. if you want promotion,. you must first find a big tree.

Your future lies not in what you have done,. but in who the person you follow is. This forms. layer upon layer of factional networks. You promote me,. I promote him,. and the whole system becomes a web of relationships. rather than a professional machine. The third root disease is also the most fatal,. and that is the complete failure of supervision. The Discipline Inspection Commission responsible for supervision. and the officials being supervised. have the same boss above their heads:. the Party (the Chinese Communist Party). This is like a football match where. the referee,. the players,. and the coach all wear the same jersey. Do you want the referee to blow the whistle and catch fouls? The ones he catches are always the opposing team. When his own people foul, he pretends not to see. So you will find. that the CCP's anti-corruption campaigns. forever carry a strong flavor of factional struggle. Anti-corruption campaigns always strike political rivals,. not corrupt officials. So what is the Founding Father's solution? It is actually the independence of the examination power. His intent is very clear:. to draw, between "political power" and "the civil service system," a line that cannot be crossed. The Party can govern,. but the Party cannot stuff its own people. into the civil service ranks. The Party can set policy direction,. but cannot order civil servants. to violate professional ethics in execution. The recruitment of civil servants,. promotion,. performance evaluation,. must be the responsibility of a constitutional organ. independent of any political party. Placed in today's context, this statement. is the sharpest knife for deconstructing. "the Party manages cadres." America's spoils division is short-term,. the CCP's Party-manages-cadres is permanent. Although the two differ in form,. the root disease is the same:. both have politics devouring professionalism. The Founding Father, over a hundred years ago,. already saw through this structural problem. Everyone has probably seen "Shaolin Soccer." There is a scene in it where it says:. the referee,. the umpire,. the linesman,. the technical committee member,. the organizer,. the co-organizer,. all the units are my people,. how can you fight against me? The Founding Father said. this was the real state. of Western parliaments at the end of the 19th century. Members of parliament are themselves political contenders. If you let them simultaneously be the referee,. to impeach executive officials,. then every whistle they blow. is based on partisan interest. The Founding Father's second knife. cut at a rarely questioned assumption. within the Western separation of three powers:. that the impeachment power and the investigative power. should, as a matter of course, belong to parliament. Britain is like this,. America is also like this. But the Founding Father said:. wait a moment. There are two big problems here. The first problem is called the weaponization of power. This thing called impeachment,. what was the original intent of its design? It is the last line of defense of the democratic system. When an official seriously breaks the law,. the people's representatives launch impeachment. to pull him down. But how does it actually work in practice? Members of parliament discovered. that the impeachment power is a very useful stick. I do not need to actually beat you out of office. I only need to raise the stick and wave it,. and you must listen to me,. let my bill pass,.

allocate funds to my district. The Founding Father called this "parliamentary tyranny." Parliament is not supervising the executive,. but extorting the executive branch. Has this phenomenon disappeared today? We look at many Latin American countries,. where the president clashes with parliament,. and parliament launches impeachment at every turn,. like Brazil and Peru,. how many presidents have been impeached in recent years. You can also look at South Korea,. where impeachment has almost become a standard procedure. that every South Korean president must go through. Even America itself,. the way impeachment cases. have been operated in the past few years. also increasingly resembles parties. tossing grenades at each other. rather than maintaining constitutional order. The Founding Father's diagnosis over a hundred years ago. is still valid today. The second problem is more fundamental:. the supervisors themselves have conflicts of interest. Who are members of parliament? They are not saints fallen from heaven. They themselves are members of political parties,. participants in political interests. If you let a player double as the referee,. how can he possibly be fair? When investigating officials of the opposing party,. he is especially diligent,. especially high-profile. If you ask him to investigate officials of his own party? Usually it is gently set down,. quietly passed over. This is not a character problem,. this is a structural problem. Because the institutional design. put the supervisors and the supervised. in the same field of interest. How can you expect him to be detached? So the Founding Father's solution is very clear:. take the supervisory power,. including impeachment, censure, and audit,. the whole set out of parliament's hands,. and set it up as an independent governing organ,. that is, the "supervisory power." This organ does not take orders from the president,. so it will not have officials shielding officials. It is also not subject to parliament,. so it will not become a weapon of vicious partisan struggle. It is simply an independent referee,. accountable only to the constitution,. accountable only to the cleanliness of the system. You can think carefully:. this design happens to form, with the people's recall power,. a "double insurance." The people watch from the outside. If you do not do well,. I use the ballot to replace you,. use recall to pull you down. This is external supervision. The Control Yuan watches from the inside. If you embezzle,. I impeach you. If you neglect your duty,. I censure you. This is internal supervision. One line of defense outside,. one line of defense inside. The two added together. can truly contain that "all-powerful government." The Founding Father's meaning is very clear:. the referee cannot place bets. If you want to supervise the government,. you must find someone who has no. political stake of their own to do it. Leaving the impeachment power in parliament. is equivalent to letting gamblers be the referee. Making the supervisory power independent. is what brings the game back to the rules. Simply put, democracy needs a referee,. but the referee cannot go onto the field to play. This is the reason the supervisory power must be independent. The Founding Father found the lesion from the West,. and also wrote the prescription. And the prescription was not fabricated out of thin air,. but came from looking back at China's own history,. discovering that our ancestors. had actually already tried something similar. Next we will talk about China's own system. As the story goes, in 1624,. during the Tianqi reign of the Ming dynasty,. a censor named Yang Lian,. knowing full well that offending Wei Zhongxian.

was equivalent to courting death,. still submitted an impeachment memorial,. listing twenty-four major crimes. As a result he was thrown into the imperial prison,. tormented to death alive. But do you know? Although he died,. the institution of the Censorate did not die. Three years later Wei Zhongxian fell,. and the whole supervisory system turned again. A single person can be killed,. but if an institution is designed firmly enough,. even eunuch dictatorship cannot crush it. What the Founding Father saw was precisely this. Is the supervisory power nostalgia or innovation? Between China's traditional censor system. and modern constitutional theory,. does there exist a logical line that connects them? Let us first return to history. The Control Yuan that the Founding Father designed,. its prototype is the Censorate and the Court of Censors. American sinologist Charles Hucker. specifically studied the Ming dynasty supervisory system. He gave it a very high evaluation,. calling it "the traditional mainstay." It means this system. is the skeleton supporting the operation of the entire empire. Hucker pointed out. that the Ming dynasty supervisory system. has three features worth noting. The first is a full-coverage monitoring network. This group of censors. had their own independent intelligence channels. In ancient China there was a saying called "speaking on hearsay," meaning I do not even. need to see ironclad evidence with my own eyes. As long as I hear word of something,. I can submit a memorial of impeachment,. and investigate afterward. From the central Six Ministries to local prefectures and counties,. the tentacles of supervision were everywhere. The second is dual function. Censors not only watched officials below,. they could also remonstrate with the emperor above. In theory he was both the inspection corps. that disciplined the officials. and the one who stepped on the brakes against monarchical power. Of course,. in practice the power of remonstrance was often discounted. But at least in institutional design,. the supervisory power had the intent to check the highest power. The third, and what most surprised Hucker,. was the resilience of the system. In the late Ming, Wei Zhongxian monopolized power,. and the eunuch faction wildly purged the censors,. killing some,. demoting some. But even in those darkest days,. the basic skeleton of the supervisory system. did not completely disintegrate. Yang Lian died,. but the institution of impeachment still existed. Individual censors were suppressed,. but the performance-evaluation mechanism still operated. After the storm passed,. the system restarted again. A system that can survive the crushing of extreme politics,. this shows that its design itself. has structural value. But here there is a fatal key point,. and that is "but." The source of power. of the traditional censor system was the emperor. The censor was "the eyes and ears of imperial power," not "the guardian of the people." When the emperor was wise,. the censor was a sharp weapon. But when the emperor was muddleheaded,. or was hollowed out by eunuchs,. the censor became a decoration, or even a sacrificial victim. The Founding Father's true innovation lies right here. He pulled this traditional organ's power cord. out of "imperial bestowal" and plugged it into "the people's bestowal," letting the legitimacy of the supervisory power. come from the constitution,. come from the people,. not from any single person. This way the nature of the whole system. went from a tool of emperors. to infrastructure of democracy. Let us talk again about another. viewpoint of contemporary Western constitutional theory. It comes from America,. from Yale Law School constitutional scholar Ackerman.

In our previous discussions of Democracy. we also introduced his viewpoint. In line with the discussion context of the supervisory power,. we still cite his viewpoint. Ackerman once published a. heavyweight legal paper named. "The New Separation of Powers." The viewpoint of this article. and the viewpoint the Founding Father proposed. 76 years before him. actually have astonishing similarities. It shows the Founding Father. had the power to penetrate across eras. Ackerman's core argument is. that the traditional separation of three powers is no longer enough. The modern state is too complex. You cannot stuff every function into. the executive,. legislative,. judicial,. three boxes. He proposed that modern constitutions. need to add two new independent branches. The first is called the "integrity branch," specifically responsible for fighting corruption. This institution must have a constitutionally guaranteed budget,. members must have a high degree of tenure protection,. and absolutely cannot be appointed solely by the president. or the executive chief. The only purpose of its existence. is to watch whether anyone in the government. is stealing,. cheating,. using power for private gain. This is almost the same blueprint. as the Founding Father's supervisory power. The second is called the "regulatory branch," specifically protecting professional decisions. from being distorted by politicians. How to do environmental protection,. how to set financial regulation,. these things need professional knowledge. You cannot let short-sighted politicians. change them recklessly for the sake of votes. So you need an independent institution. to hold the professional bottom line. This is the examination power. The spirit of the examination power. is not just holding examinations,. but ensuring that "governing power" is held. in the hands of people who truly have professional ability,. not contaminated by political force. Two people,. two eras,. two completely different intellectual traditions,. yet drew almost identical institutional blueprints. The Founding Father in 1924. proposed the Five-Power Constitution. Ackerman in 2000,. from the predicament of contemporary democracy,. deduced a new separation-of-powers theory. The two reached the same conclusion by different paths. In academic language,. the Five-Power Constitution is actually. a pioneer of "functional separation of powers." What he wanted to do is very clear:. take the two functions a modern state most needs,. "professionalism" and "integrity," pull them out of the chaotic political mudslinging,. and put them into a constitutional-level safe box. The Ming dynasty's Yang Lian. used his life to protect the dignity of the censors,. but he could not protect the root of the institution,. because that root was planted in the soil of imperial power. What the Founding Father did. was uproot the same tree. and transplant it into the soil of contemporary democracy. Ackerman, 76 years later,. came from a completely different direction. and planted an almost identical tree. The same answer was, by two eras,. two civilizations' thinkers,. each independently deduced. This is not coincidence but inevitability. The independent guarantee of professionalism and integrity. is a necessity of the modern state. Because the Three Principles of the People. are actually very much worth discussing,. but the content is really too much. We will discuss in the next episode. the unique institutional design of the "Five-Power Constitution," that is, the examination power and the supervisory power,. and will also introduce their practical experience in Taiwan,. hoping to make a modest contribution to how a future China,. after democratization, should carry out constitutional design.

If you enjoyed this episode,. please like,. subscribe, and share it. So we will see you next time. Bye bye!

值得閱讀的理由

  • 深刻剖析孫中山五權憲法獨立考試權與監察權的憲政遠見，理解制度防腐與品質管控的必要性。
  • 以1881年美國總統加菲爾遇刺案為例，透析早期西方民主分贓制（獵官制）引發的體制災難與文官改革歷程。
  • 對比當前中共「黨管幹部」的政治運作，揭示政治忠誠凌駕專業理性所帶來的深層治理浩劫。

摘要

民主機器的隱患與五權憲法的防腐機制

作者藉由超跑與遙控器的生動比喻指出，人民手中握有選舉、罷免、創制、複決等權利，如同持有高級跑車的遙控器，但若政府機器內部零件粗製濫造、滿布鏽斑，僅憑選民的控制依然無法防止車輛失控。國父早在百餘年前便洞悉此一問題，認為僅有西方傳統的三權分立仍有漏洞，因而提出將考試權與監察權獨立出來。考試權負責政府人才的品質把關，監察權則負責內部的防腐監督。作者強調，此一見解與現代憲政學者艾克曼的理論不謀而合，證明了民主不僅是投票制度，更需要一套實質的防腐劑與穩定器。

美國「獵官制」的歷史悲劇與三大災難

作者回顧了1881年美國總統加菲爾遇刺身亡的歷史慘劇，直指其背後的罪魁禍首正是惡名昭彰的分贓制。在早期美國政治中，「勝者全拿官職」成為潛規則，競選功臣與金主得以瓜分內閣及各級官職。作者引述國父的分析，點出該體制造成的「三大災難」：其一是效能週期性崩潰，每次政黨輪替導致政府如走馬燈般陷入混亂；其二是逆向淘汰，選邊站的政客取代了具備專業能力的專家；其三則是體制性腐敗，公職淪為政治投資的籌碼，官員只向賜官的政黨效忠而非國家。雖然美國隨後在1883年通過《彭德爾頓法案》設立文官委員會，但國父認為文官系統若受制於行政權，防火牆終究存在後門，必須拉高至憲法位階才能徹底杜絕分贓。

從分贓制到極權實踐：現代「黨管幹部」的代價

作者進一步將歷史上的獵官制延伸對照當今中共體制，指出其「黨管幹部」本質上是更徹底、全面且永久的政治恩庇。從政府、國企到學術機構，所有核心職位皆由黨組織掌控分配。雖然這種模式看似避免了定期輪替造成的行政中斷，但其穩定背後付出的代價極其高昂。首要病灶便是專業理性被扼殺，當「政治忠誠」成為升遷首要考量，技術官僚的專業判斷被迫屈服於領袖意志，導致如大躍進或動態清零等重大決策失誤；其次則是派系依附取代制度理性，徹底扭曲了健全官僚體系的運作。

================================================

Hello! Everyone. This is A-Niu. The third part of "Lecture Six on Democracy." In the previous two episodes we finished discussing. "the distinction between power and ability." To understand it better,. let us give an example. You just bought a supercar,. holding the remote control of this car in your hand. You can start it at any time,. turn it off at any time. But if you open the hood and look,. and to your surprise the engine parts are all made of plastic,. the oil lines full of rust,. would you still dare to step on the gas? What we want to ask today is:. relying only on the remote control in the people's hands,. can it really guarantee that the. "all-powerful government" will not have problems? The Founding Father actually, over 100 years ago,. already saw this problem. He said. that the people having election,. recall,. initiative,. and referendum is not enough. Why? First,. if the people who go into the government to do the work. got in by connections,. then the parts of this machine. are inferior goods from the day they leave the factory. Second,. if inside the machine. no one continuously monitors or supervises,. then corruption and malpractice, like rust,. will slowly corrode the entire circuit from the inside. By the time the people feel something is wrong. and want to press the remote control,. this car may long ago have been unable to brake. So he pulled the "examination" and "supervisory" powers. out of the traditional three powers (executive, legislative, judicial). to stand independently. The examination power is responsible for quality control,. ensuring that the people entering the government. have real talent and learning. The supervisory power is responsible. for rust-proofing or anti-corrosion,. continuously monitoring and supervising inside the government. But you might think,. isn't this just nostalgia? Taking China's traditional imperial examinations,. the censorate, and such systems,. and moving them into modern politics. But the core of the problem he truly aimed at. was two loopholes that 19th-century Western democracy. exposed. The prescription he himself wrote. The interesting thing is. that in the year 2000,. American constitutional scholar Ackerman. was almost completely consistent. with this logic of the Founding Father. We can put it this way:. democracy is not just a voting system. It also needs a set of anti-corrosives and stabilizers. This is, in the Five-Power Constitution,. the most underrated insight. So what exactly did the Founding Father see back then. in terms of the ills of Western democracy? As the story goes, in 1881,. the American president took a train to the station,. and a man who had failed to obtain office pulled out a gun. The then American president Garfield was assassinated. This was not a random killing,. but a tragedy caused by a. "spoils system." Someone treated public office like a lottery ticket,. and when they could not cash in the prize,. they poured their rage into bullets. A system so rotten. that it made people risk their lives to grab official posts. I think this kind of tragedy. is one no one wants to happen. Let us examine carefully. the institutional problem. behind the American president's assassination. How exactly did America's "spoils system" operate? When the Founding Father gave his lectures,. he spent great effort on one thing:. performing a pathological dissection of Western democracy. His attitude was not anti-democracy,. but rather to say:.

your separation of three powers has loopholes,. and I want to patch up the loopholes. The first disease is America's "spoils system." What is the spoils system? In plain terms it is:. win the election,. and all the official posts in the country. are the president's spoils of war,. rewarded according to merit and distributed to his own people. This way of playing,. in the era when Jackson served as American president,. became an explicit rule. Their slogan was:. "To the victor belong the spoils." What does it mean? You help me canvass votes to win the presidency,. and I give you a lucrative customs post. You donate a lot of money,. and I make you the postmaster. From cabinet ministers to minor local officials,. all are spoils the president distributes down. The Founding Father observed that this system. would bring three disasters. The first disaster. is called the periodic collapse of effectiveness. A general election is held every 4 years. No matter who is elected,. the government gets a major blood transfusion. The newly arrived people do not understand the business at all,. and before they have even figured out which way the door opens,. the next term must change people again. In his lecture he gave a metaphor:. the government spins like a revolving lantern,. forever in handover,. forever in chaos. The second disaster is called "reverse elimination." What kind of people can become officials? Not the most capable people,. but the people best at picking sides. No matter how strong your professional ability,. if you have no party card,. you cannot even get in the door. Conversely,. those old hands in the politician circles,. the election campaign fixers,. sit down in the offices one by one. The Founding Father's principle is very clear:. governing power should be given to experts,. not to loyal followers. The third disaster is the most serious,. and that is systemic corruption. Think about it. If a person's official post. is a gift given by the party,. to whom will they be accountable after taking office? To the party,. accountable to their benefactor,. not to the country,. accountable to the law. And to get this post,. they may have spent a sum of money to "buy" it. So what will they do after taking office? Of course, recover that money. Public office becomes an investment target,. and corruption goes from an individual case. to the normal state of the entire system. This spoils system, later on,. the Americans really could not stand it. So,. after that presidential assassination in 1881,. it ultimately forced out the pressure for necessary reform. In 1883,. the US Congress passed the "Pendleton Act," establishing the Civil Service Commission. and beginning to adopt a system. of selecting talent through examinations. However, after the Founding Father looked at it, he said. this was not enough. Why? Because your Civil Service Commission. is a bureau hung under the executive branch. The president still has ways to apply pressure,. the ruling party still has channels to stuff in its own people. If the examination power. does not break away from the executive power. to independently become a. constitutional organ parallel to. the executive,. judicial, and legislative powers,. then the firewall will forever have a back door. That gunshot in America. also shattered a myth:. that relying on elections alone can produce good government. But the Founding Father actually saw farther than the Americans. He wanted not only a "merit system,"

but to upgrade the merit system into. a constitutional-level institutional firewall,. so that no political party could treat the civil service system. as its own backyard garden. In short,. elections decide who drives the car,. but examinations decide. how this car's parts are assembled. If you give the power to build the car to elections,. then sooner or later you will sit in a useless cobbled-together car. Although in the 19th century. America's spoils system was already outrageous,. even today in the 21st century. there are still people who play this way of doing things. to the extreme. Permanently,. comprehensively dividing the spoils. From government to enterprises to schools,. all sectors are dividing the spoils. As long as you are not a party member,. you cannot get a share of the pie. If the spoils system is permanent,. comprehensive,. distributed from the central government. down to the neighborhood committee at the end of your alley,. from the chairman of a state-owned enterprise down. to the university president,. what kind of scene would that be? No need to imagine. This system is operating today. It even has an official name,. called "the Party manages cadres." Is the CCP's "Party manages cadres" essentially the same thing as. America's early spoils system? When the Founding Father. criticized America's spoils system back then,. the core concept he used. can be summarized in four characters:. political patronage. It means. your official post was not earned by ability,. but bestowed on you by political power. To whom are you loyal? Loyal to the person who gave you the post. The American version is that you win the election. before you can divide the spoils. Four years later it may have to be reshuffled. But the CCP's version is more thorough. It does not need elections,. one party rules permanently. So the division of spoils is not a one-time thing,. it is a normal state written into the system. All key positions:. government,. enterprises,. schools,. social organizations,. are all inspected and appointed. by the Party's Organization Department. Of course you might say. at least this system is stable,. it will not have a major blood. transfusion every four years like America. Correct. It indeed avoids the problem of administrative interruption. But what is the price of stability? There are at least three deeper root diseases. The first root disease is. that professional rationality is smothered alive. When "political loyalty" becomes the first metric of assessment,. the professional judgment of technical bureaucrats. must give way to political directives. When the experts say no. and the leader says yes,. who should be obeyed? Of course, obey the leader. As a result,. the Great Leap Forward of 1958 came about this way. The dynamic-zero policy during the pandemic. also came about this way. It is not that no one saw the problem,. it is that even if someone saw the problem, they dared not speak,. or were disappeared. Because if you spoke up, you were no longer loyal. The second root disease is. that factional dependence replaces institutional rationality. In a normal modern bureaucratic system,. promotion relies on performance,. on rules,. on "impersonal" standards. But in the Party-manages-cadres system,. if you want promotion,. you must first find a big tree.

Your future lies not in what you have done,. but in who the person you follow is. This forms. layer upon layer of factional networks. You promote me,. I promote him,. and the whole system becomes a web of relationships. rather than a professional machine. The third root disease is also the most fatal,. and that is the complete failure of supervision. The Discipline Inspection Commission responsible for supervision. and the officials being supervised. have the same boss above their heads:. the Party (the Chinese Communist Party). This is like a football match where. the referee,. the players,. and the coach all wear the same jersey. Do you want the referee to blow the whistle and catch fouls? The ones he catches are always the opposing team. When his own people foul, he pretends not to see. So you will find. that the CCP's anti-corruption campaigns. forever carry a strong flavor of factional struggle. Anti-corruption campaigns always strike political rivals,. not corrupt officials. So what is the Founding Father's solution? It is actually the independence of the examination power. His intent is very clear:. to draw, between "political power" and "the civil service system," a line that cannot be crossed. The Party can govern,. but the Party cannot stuff its own people. into the civil service ranks. The Party can set policy direction,. but cannot order civil servants. to violate professional ethics in execution. The recruitment of civil servants,. promotion,. performance evaluation,. must be the responsibility of a constitutional organ. independent of any political party. Placed in today's context, this statement. is the sharpest knife for deconstructing. "the Party manages cadres." America's spoils division is short-term,. the CCP's Party-manages-cadres is permanent. Although the two differ in form,. the root disease is the same:. both have politics devouring professionalism. The Founding Father, over a hundred years ago,. already saw through this structural problem. Everyone has probably seen "Shaolin Soccer." There is a scene in it where it says:. the referee,. the umpire,. the linesman,. the technical committee member,. the organizer,. the co-organizer,. all the units are my people,. how can you fight against me? The Founding Father said. this was the real state. of Western parliaments at the end of the 19th century. Members of parliament are themselves political contenders. If you let them simultaneously be the referee,. to impeach executive officials,. then every whistle they blow. is based on partisan interest. The Founding Father's second knife. cut at a rarely questioned assumption. within the Western separation of three powers:. that the impeachment power and the investigative power. should, as a matter of course, belong to parliament. Britain is like this,. America is also like this. But the Founding Father said:. wait a moment. There are two big problems here. The first problem is called the weaponization of power. This thing called impeachment,. what was the original intent of its design? It is the last line of defense of the democratic system. When an official seriously breaks the law,. the people's representatives launch impeachment. to pull him down. But how does it actually work in practice? Members of parliament discovered. that the impeachment power is a very useful stick. I do not need to actually beat you out of office. I only need to raise the stick and wave it,. and you must listen to me,. let my bill pass,.

allocate funds to my district. The Founding Father called this "parliamentary tyranny." Parliament is not supervising the executive,. but extorting the executive branch. Has this phenomenon disappeared today? We look at many Latin American countries,. where the president clashes with parliament,. and parliament launches impeachment at every turn,. like Brazil and Peru,. how many presidents have been impeached in recent years. You can also look at South Korea,. where impeachment has almost become a standard procedure. that every South Korean president must go through. Even America itself,. the way impeachment cases. have been operated in the past few years. also increasingly resembles parties. tossing grenades at each other. rather than maintaining constitutional order. The Founding Father's diagnosis over a hundred years ago. is still valid today. The second problem is more fundamental:. the supervisors themselves have conflicts of interest. Who are members of parliament? They are not saints fallen from heaven. They themselves are members of political parties,. participants in political interests. If you let a player double as the referee,. how can he possibly be fair? When investigating officials of the opposing party,. he is especially diligent,. especially high-profile. If you ask him to investigate officials of his own party? Usually it is gently set down,. quietly passed over. This is not a character problem,. this is a structural problem. Because the institutional design. put the supervisors and the supervised. in the same field of interest. How can you expect him to be detached? So the Founding Father's solution is very clear:. take the supervisory power,. including impeachment, censure, and audit,. the whole set out of parliament's hands,. and set it up as an independent governing organ,. that is, the "supervisory power." This organ does not take orders from the president,. so it will not have officials shielding officials. It is also not subject to parliament,. so it will not become a weapon of vicious partisan struggle. It is simply an independent referee,. accountable only to the constitution,. accountable only to the cleanliness of the system. You can think carefully:. this design happens to form, with the people's recall power,. a "double insurance." The people watch from the outside. If you do not do well,. I use the ballot to replace you,. use recall to pull you down. This is external supervision. The Control Yuan watches from the inside. If you embezzle,. I impeach you. If you neglect your duty,. I censure you. This is internal supervision. One line of defense outside,. one line of defense inside. The two added together. can truly contain that "all-powerful government." The Founding Father's meaning is very clear:. the referee cannot place bets. If you want to supervise the government,. you must find someone who has no. political stake of their own to do it. Leaving the impeachment power in parliament. is equivalent to letting gamblers be the referee. Making the supervisory power independent. is what brings the game back to the rules. Simply put, democracy needs a referee,. but the referee cannot go onto the field to play. This is the reason the supervisory power must be independent. The Founding Father found the lesion from the West,. and also wrote the prescription. And the prescription was not fabricated out of thin air,. but came from looking back at China's own history,. discovering that our ancestors. had actually already tried something similar. Next we will talk about China's own system. As the story goes, in 1624,. during the Tianqi reign of the Ming dynasty,. a censor named Yang Lian,. knowing full well that offending Wei Zhongxian.

was equivalent to courting death,. still submitted an impeachment memorial,. listing twenty-four major crimes. As a result he was thrown into the imperial prison,. tormented to death alive. But do you know? Although he died,. the institution of the Censorate did not die. Three years later Wei Zhongxian fell,. and the whole supervisory system turned again. A single person can be killed,. but if an institution is designed firmly enough,. even eunuch dictatorship cannot crush it. What the Founding Father saw was precisely this. Is the supervisory power nostalgia or innovation? Between China's traditional censor system. and modern constitutional theory,. does there exist a logical line that connects them? Let us first return to history. The Control Yuan that the Founding Father designed,. its prototype is the Censorate and the Court of Censors. American sinologist Charles Hucker. specifically studied the Ming dynasty supervisory system. He gave it a very high evaluation,. calling it "the traditional mainstay." It means this system. is the skeleton supporting the operation of the entire empire. Hucker pointed out. that the Ming dynasty supervisory system. has three features worth noting. The first is a full-coverage monitoring network. This group of censors. had their own independent intelligence channels. In ancient China there was a saying called "speaking on hearsay," meaning I do not even. need to see ironclad evidence with my own eyes. As long as I hear word of something,. I can submit a memorial of impeachment,. and investigate afterward. From the central Six Ministries to local prefectures and counties,. the tentacles of supervision were everywhere. The second is dual function. Censors not only watched officials below,. they could also remonstrate with the emperor above. In theory he was both the inspection corps. that disciplined the officials. and the one who stepped on the brakes against monarchical power. Of course,. in practice the power of remonstrance was often discounted. But at least in institutional design,. the supervisory power had the intent to check the highest power. The third, and what most surprised Hucker,. was the resilience of the system. In the late Ming, Wei Zhongxian monopolized power,. and the eunuch faction wildly purged the censors,. killing some,. demoting some. But even in those darkest days,. the basic skeleton of the supervisory system. did not completely disintegrate. Yang Lian died,. but the institution of impeachment still existed. Individual censors were suppressed,. but the performance-evaluation mechanism still operated. After the storm passed,. the system restarted again. A system that can survive the crushing of extreme politics,. this shows that its design itself. has structural value. But here there is a fatal key point,. and that is "but." The source of power. of the traditional censor system was the emperor. The censor was "the eyes and ears of imperial power," not "the guardian of the people." When the emperor was wise,. the censor was a sharp weapon. But when the emperor was muddleheaded,. or was hollowed out by eunuchs,. the censor became a decoration, or even a sacrificial victim. The Founding Father's true innovation lies right here. He pulled this traditional organ's power cord. out of "imperial bestowal" and plugged it into "the people's bestowal," letting the legitimacy of the supervisory power. come from the constitution,. come from the people,. not from any single person. This way the nature of the whole system. went from a tool of emperors. to infrastructure of democracy. Let us talk again about another. viewpoint of contemporary Western constitutional theory. It comes from America,. from Yale Law School constitutional scholar Ackerman.

In our previous discussions of Democracy. we also introduced his viewpoint. In line with the discussion context of the supervisory power,. we still cite his viewpoint. Ackerman once published a. heavyweight legal paper named. "The New Separation of Powers." The viewpoint of this article. and the viewpoint the Founding Father proposed. 76 years before him. actually have astonishing similarities. It shows the Founding Father. had the power to penetrate across eras. Ackerman's core argument is. that the traditional separation of three powers is no longer enough. The modern state is too complex. You cannot stuff every function into. the executive,. legislative,. judicial,. three boxes. He proposed that modern constitutions. need to add two new independent branches. The first is called the "integrity branch," specifically responsible for fighting corruption. This institution must have a constitutionally guaranteed budget,. members must have a high degree of tenure protection,. and absolutely cannot be appointed solely by the president. or the executive chief. The only purpose of its existence. is to watch whether anyone in the government. is stealing,. cheating,. using power for private gain. This is almost the same blueprint. as the Founding Father's supervisory power. The second is called the "regulatory branch," specifically protecting professional decisions. from being distorted by politicians. How to do environmental protection,. how to set financial regulation,. these things need professional knowledge. You cannot let short-sighted politicians. change them recklessly for the sake of votes. So you need an independent institution. to hold the professional bottom line. This is the examination power. The spirit of the examination power. is not just holding examinations,. but ensuring that "governing power" is held. in the hands of people who truly have professional ability,. not contaminated by political force. Two people,. two eras,. two completely different intellectual traditions,. yet drew almost identical institutional blueprints. The Founding Father in 1924. proposed the Five-Power Constitution. Ackerman in 2000,. from the predicament of contemporary democracy,. deduced a new separation-of-powers theory. The two reached the same conclusion by different paths. In academic language,. the Five-Power Constitution is actually. a pioneer of "functional separation of powers." What he wanted to do is very clear:. take the two functions a modern state most needs,. "professionalism" and "integrity," pull them out of the chaotic political mudslinging,. and put them into a constitutional-level safe box. The Ming dynasty's Yang Lian. used his life to protect the dignity of the censors,. but he could not protect the root of the institution,. because that root was planted in the soil of imperial power. What the Founding Father did. was uproot the same tree. and transplant it into the soil of contemporary democracy. Ackerman, 76 years later,. came from a completely different direction. and planted an almost identical tree. The same answer was, by two eras,. two civilizations' thinkers,. each independently deduced. This is not coincidence but inevitability. The independent guarantee of professionalism and integrity. is a necessity of the modern state. Because the Three Principles of the People. are actually very much worth discussing,. but the content is really too much.
